text: Not the height, it is the declivity that is terrible!
plain: Climbing isn't the scary part. The drop below you is.

text: The greatest events—are not our noisiest, but our stillest hours.
plain: What matters most happens quietly, not in the loud moments.

text: Not around the inventors of new noise, but around the inventors of new values, doth the world revolve; INAUDIBLY it revolveth.
plain: The world turns around people who change what we value, not around whoever is loudest.

text: To redeem what is past, and to transform every “It was” into “Thus would I have it!”—that only do I call redemption!
plain: You can't change what happened, but you can own it and decide it was what you wanted.

text: Not backward can the Will will; that it cannot break time and time’s desire—that is the Will’s lonesomest tribulation.
plain: Revenge is rage at the fact that time only runs forward.

text: Freedom do I love, and the air over fresh soil; rather would I sleep on ox-skins than on their honours and dignities.
plain: I'd take a rough bed and my freedom over titles that come with strings.

text: Dare only to believe in yourselves—in yourselves and in your inward parts! He who doth not believe in himself always lieth.
plain: If you don't trust yourself, you end up lying to everyone, yourself first.

text: This is my first manly prudence, that I allow myself to be deceived, so as not to be on my guard against deceivers.
plain: Getting burned sometimes beats living guarded against everyone.

text: And he who would not languish amongst men, must learn to drink out of all glasses; and he who would keep clean amongst men, must know how to wash himself even with dirty water.
plain: To live among people without going sour, take them as they are and stay clean anyway.

text: Is not wounded vanity the mother of all tragedies? Where, however, pride is wounded, there groweth up something better than pride.
plain: A bruised ego causes most disasters. A bruised pride can grow into something real.

text: Loving and perishing: these have rhymed from eternity. Will to love: that is to be ready also for death.
plain: Loving anything means accepting you can lose it.

text: Verily, even for dying have we become too weary; now do we keep awake and live on—in sepulchres.
plain: Some exhaustion is so deep you're not living, just lingering in your own grave.

text: To execute great things is difficult: but the more difficult task is to command great things.
plain: Doing the work is hard. Having the nerve to lead it is harder.

text: What matter about their mockery! Thou art one who hast unlearned to obey: now shalt thou command!
plain: Their mockery is nothing. You've outgrown taking orders, so lead.

text: The dew falleth on the grass when the night is most silent.
plain: Growth lands in the quiet hours, when it looks like nothing is happening.

text: It is the stillest words which bring the storm. Thoughts that come with doves’ footsteps guide the world.
plain: The quiet ideas are the ones that end up steering everything.

text: O Zarathustra, thy fruits are ripe, but thou art not ripe for thy fruits!
plain: The work is ready before you are. Go grow into it.

text: We also know too little, and are bad learners: so we are obliged to lie.
plain: When we don't know enough, we bluff.

text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness: it must now be thy best courage that there is no longer any path behind thee!
plain: No way back is your best weapon. Now you have to go forward.

text: And if all ladders henceforth fail thee, then must thou learn to mount upon thine own head: how couldst thou mount upward otherwise?
plain: When every ladder breaks, you climb on your own head. There's no other way up.

text: Now must the gentlest in thee become the hardest.
plain: The soft part of you has to get tough now.

text: He who hath always much-indulged himself, sickeneth at last by his much-indulgence.
plain: Spoil yourself long enough and it makes you sick.

text: Out of the deepest must the highest come to its height.
plain: The highest peaks rise from the lowest depths. Your worst stretch is what you climb from.

text: LOVE is the danger of the lonesomest one, love to anything, IF IT ONLY LIVE!
plain: When you're lonely, you'll love anything that moves, and that is the trap.

text: Courage, however, is the best slayer, courage which attacketh: it slayeth even death itself; for it saith: “WAS THAT life? Well! Once more!”
plain: Courage kills fear of death by looking at life and saying: again.

text: Courage slayeth also giddiness at abysses: and where doth man not stand at abysses! Is not seeing itself—seeing abysses?
plain: Everyone stands at an edge somewhere. Looking clearly means seeing the drop.

text: In their hearts they want simply one thing most of all: that no one hurt them.
plain: Most people mainly want to avoid getting hurt, and they call that virtue.

text: Ye ever become smaller, ye small people! Ye crumble away, ye comfortable ones!
plain: Comfort shrinks you a little more every day.

text: Too tender, too yielding: so is your soil! But for a tree to become GREAT, it seeketh to twine hard roots around hard rocks!
plain: Big things grow where the ground is hard. Soft soil makes small trees.

text: Ah, that ye would renounce all HALF-willing, and would decide for idleness as ye decide for action!
plain: Quit the half-effort. Either rest fully or act fully.

text: Do ever what ye will—but first be such as CAN WILL.
plain: Do what you want, but first become someone with a real will.

text: With a wickedness do I begin every day: I mock at the winter with a cold bath: on that account grumbleth my stern house-mate.
plain: Start the day by doing the hard thing on purpose, cold bath and all.

text: A poor bed warmeth me more than a rich one, for I am jealous of my poverty. And in winter she is most faithful unto me.
plain: Being broke can be a friend that keeps you hungry and honest.

text: Never in my life did I creep before the powerful; and if ever I lied, then did I lie out of love.
plain: I never groveled to anyone with power.

text: To one man, lonesomeness is the flight of the sick one; to another, it is the flight FROM the sick ones.
plain: Being alone can be running away from life or running away from the people draining it.

text: They hound one another, and know not whither! They inflame one another, and know not why!
plain: The crowd rushes and fights with no idea where it is going.

text: They are cold, and seek warmth from distilled waters: they are inflamed, and seek coolness from frozen spirits; they are all sick and sore through public opinion.
plain: Public opinion makes people sick, and they chase the wrong cures.

text: This precept, however, give I unto thee, in parting, thou fool: Where one can no longer love, there should one—PASS BY!
plain: Where you can't love anymore, walk past. Don't waste time on the fight.

text: The half-and-half spoil every whole.
plain: Half-committed people ruin the whole thing.

text: One thing is forsakenness, another matter is lonesomeness: THAT hast thou now learned!
plain: Being abandoned and choosing solitude are different things.

text: Everything among them talketh; no one knoweth any longer how to understand. Everything falleth into the water; nothing falleth any longer into deep wells.
plain: Everyone talks and nothing sinks in deep.

text: Everything among them talketh, nothing succeedeth any longer and accomplisheth itself. Everything cackleth, but who will still sit quietly on the nest and hatch eggs?
plain: Everyone is loud, few sit still long enough to finish anything.

text: He who liveth amongst the good—pity teacheth him to lie. Pity maketh stifling air for all free souls.
plain: Constant pity makes you lie to be gentle, and it smothers free people.

text: Thereof could I sing a song—and WILL sing it: though I be alone in an empty house, and must sing it to mine own ears.
plain: I'll make the thing even if the room is empty and the only audience is me.

text: One must learn to love oneself—thus do I teach—with a wholesome and healthy love: that one may endure to be with oneself, and not go roving about.
plain: Learn to like your own company so you stop running from it.

text: This however is my teaching: he who wisheth one day to fly, must first learn standing and walking and running and climbing and dancing:—one doth not fly into flying!
plain: No skipping steps. You walk, run, and climb before you fly.

text: “This—is now MY way,—where is yours?” Thus did I answer those who asked me “the way.” For THE way—it doth not exist!
plain: There's no one right path. Find yours.

text: But man himself only is hard to bear! The reason thereof is that he carrieth too many extraneous things on his shoulders.
plain: Life feels heavy because you carry other people's rules and words.

text: He who cannot command himself shall obey. And many a one CAN command himself, but still sorely lacketh self-obedience!
plain: If you can't rule yourself, someone else will. And giving orders to yourself isn't enough, you have to follow them.

text: Let it not be your honour henceforth whence ye come, but whither ye go!
plain: Where you came from doesn't count. Where you're headed does.

text: The daring venture, the prolonged distrust, the cruel Nay, the tedium, the cutting-into-the-quick—how seldom do THESE come together! Out of such seed, however—is truth produced!
plain: Truth comes from risk, doubt, saying no, boredom, and pain. Few stick with all of it.

text: In the best there is still something to loathe; and the best is still something that must be surpassed!
plain: Even your best has flaws, and even your best is something to beat.

text: Willing emancipateth: for willing is creating: so do I teach.
plain: Deciding what you want frees you, because wanting is how things get made.

text: And such is always the nature of weak men: they lose themselves on their way. And at last asketh their weariness: “Why did we ever go on the way? All is indifferent!”
plain: People who go soft lose the thread, then call the whole trip pointless.

text: Only a span-breadth is he from his goal; but from weariness hath he lain down obstinately in the dust, this brave one!
plain: He quit a hand's width from the finish because he was tired.

text: I love the brave: but it is not enough to be a swordsman,—one must also know WHEREON to use swordsmanship!
plain: Being tough isn't enough. Know what is worth fighting.

text: And lost be the day to us in which a measure hath not been danced. And false be every truth which hath not had laughter along with it!
plain: A day without joy is a lost day, and a truth with no laughter in it is suspect.

text: Why so soft, so submissive and yielding? Why is there so much negation and abnegation in your hearts? Why is there so little fate in your looks?
plain: You have gone too soft to want anything big. Get some destiny back in your eyes.

text: This new table, O my brethren, put I up over you: BECOME HARD!
plain: Stop going easy on yourself. Toughen up where it counts.

text: O thou, my Will! Thou change of every need, MY needfulness! Preserve me from all small victories!
plain: Don't let a small win make you stop short of the big thing.

text: Everything goeth, everything returneth; eternally rolleth the wheel of existence. Everything dieth, everything blossometh forth again; eternally runneth on the year of existence.
plain: Everything ends and starts again. The wheel keeps turning.

text: Woe unto all loving ones who have not an elevation which is above their pity!
plain: Love without a spine above its pity does damage.
